Blackstone pays a variable 4.88% yield tied to distributable earnings, while Franklin Templeton has raised its quarterly dividend every year since 2020.

Invesco's QQQ conversion to an open-end fund generated $130 million in new management fee revenue in just the first half of the year.

Franklin Templeton ranks first for dividend safety, Invesco second with the strongest adjusted earnings coverage, and Blackstone last despite paying the highest yield.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

Blackstone (NYSE:BX) reported this morning that profit fell as rates, inflation, and a choppy market slowed dealmaking and investment exits (Bloomberg, Reuters). Investors still bought the stock, sending shares up 4.04% in early trading. That reaction explains why this group of stocks works for income investors. Asset managers collect fees on the money they manage, so rising markets lift assets, fees, and the cash that pays dividends. Blackstone, Franklin Templeton (NYSE:BEN) and Invesco (NYSE:IVZ) all pay their dividends from that fee engine, but each one sets its payout in a very different way.

VideoFlow / Shutterstock.com
How Asset Managers Turn Market Rallies Into Dividend Checks

An asset manager charges a small percentage fee on its assets under management (AUM). When stock and bond prices rise, AUM grows even if no new client money comes in, and fee revenue grows with it. At Invesco, the CFO said favorable markets alone added $257 billion to AUM last quarter. Alternative managers like Blackstone also earn performance fees and carried interest when they sell investments at a gain.

That income depends most on the market, because profitable exits need open IPO and M&A windows. It works in reverse too. Falling markets shrink AUM and fees, which is why all three stocks carry betas above 1.5: 1.587 for Blackstone, 1.576 for Franklin and 1.631 for Invesco.

Blackstone pays out about 85% of its distributable earnings each quarter, so the check changes every time. The last three payments were $1.49, $1.16, and $1.29.

IonQ's quantum-computing peers did worse. D-Wave Quantum (NASDAQ:QBTS) stock is down 35% over the past month to $11.49, and Rigetti Computing (NASDAQ:RGTI) stock is down 31% to $11.38. Those larger losses suggest that the selloff runs deeper than IonQ's own issues.

Broader baskets held up better. The Defiance Quantum ETF (NASDAQ:QTUM) is down 11% over the past month, and the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 5%, marking pure-play quantum stocks as the market's weak spot.

IONQ Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
October Deals Fuel Dilution Fears

IonQ agreed on October 12 to buy cybersecurity company Elisity in an all-stock deal. On October 14, it launched a large equity offering, raising dilution concerns.

IonQ builds trapped-ion quantum computers and has been buying networking and security businesses, and each stock-funded deal reduces holders' ownership.

D-Wave and Rigetti Fell Even Harder Than IonQ

D-Wave sells quantum annealing systems and cloud access, while Rigetti builds superconducting chips, giving each company a technical approach distinct from IonQ's. Those differences didn't shield either stock, pointing to pressure across quantum pure plays as a group.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 22, 2026) - Questcorp Mining Inc. (CSE: QQQ) (OTCQB: QQCMF) (FSE: D910) (the "Company" or "Questcorp") has reached an agreement (the "Agreement") to complete its option exercise (the "Option") and acquire the remaining forty-nine percent interest in the North Island Copper Project (the "Project"), bringing its ownership to 100% upon completion.

The North Island Copper Project consists of a series of mineral claims, totalling approximately 1,168 hectares, located near Port Hardy on Vancouver Island, British Columbia. The Company currently holds a fifty-one percent interest in the Project and has the Option to acquire the remaining forty-nine percent interest from the current owner (the "Vendor").

Pursuant to the Agreement, the Company intends to exercise the Option and acquire the remaining forty-nine percent interest in the Project by completing a final cash payment of $110,000 and issuing 250,000 common shares (the "Consideration Shares") to the Vendor. Following exercise of the Option, the Company will hold a one-hundred percent interest in the Project and will grant to the Vendor a three percent net smelter returns royalty (the "Royalty") on commercial production from the Project. The Company may acquire the first one percent of the Royalty by completing a cash payment of $750,000, and may acquire the remaining two percent of the Royalty for an additional $1,000,000.

The Consideration Shares will be subject to restrictions on resale for a period of four-months-and-one-day in accordance with applicable securities laws. The Company is at arms-length from the Vendor, and its principal. Completion of the exercise the Option remains subject to applicable regulatory approvals.

About Questcorp Mining Inc.

Questcorp Mining Inc. is engaged in the business of the acquisition and exploration of mineral properties in North America, with the objective of locating and developing economic precious and base metals properties of merit. The Company holds an option to acquire an undivided 100% interest in and to mineral claims totaling 1,168.09 hectares comprising the North Island Copper Property, on Vancouver Island, British Columbia, subject to a royalty obligation. The Company also holds an option to acquire an undivided 100% interest in and to mineral claims totaling 2,520.2 hectares comprising the La Union Project located in Sonora, Mexico, subject to a royalty obligation.
